articles.chapeau: Users were briefly able to leave GTA 6 reviews on Metacritic.
articles.txt:
Fake user reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 have already been spotted on Metacritic, days before the game is set to launch.
Some of these were negative reviews, bringing the overall user score down before anyone has had a chance to play the game.
Metacritic has already removed these user reviews and has blocked anyone from making any more. Typically, the site blocks user reviews until a game has been out for at least 36 hours, to prevent review bombings from those who haven’t played it.
Metacritic acted quickly here, so it will likely be keeping an eye on launch. It has already tried to curb the issue of review bombing in the past, introducing the aforementioned wait times until users can leave their reviews.
Given all of the attention on GTA 6, it isn’t surprising to see that it’s already being targeted for review bombing. It feels like the industry has ground to a halt as we wait for GTA 6 to launch, something which many in the gaming community appear to resent. However, this will likely be reversed when the game launches, given all of the excitement surrounding this release.
As we inch closer to November 19, the excitement has only ramped up. The game’s map may have leaked early as part of an official merch drop and was quickly shared online by those looking for any bits of information they can get their hands on. Many fans will also be using the ‘New Zealand’ trick to play GTA 6 early, changing their console’s location to New Zealand so they can be amongst the first to boot the game up.
GTA 6 launches on PlayStation and Xbox on November 19. A PC port is expected at a later date.

La boite ne contient en effet aucun disque, seulement un code d’activation pour le PlayStation Store ou le Xbox Store.
Impossible de jouer avant le 19 novembre, sauf pour les joueurs Xbox qui pourront régler leur console pour jouer dès mercredi midi .
La boite de GTA 6 contient uniquement le poster officiel du jeu, un feuillet pour expliquer comment télécharger le jeu et un feuillet faisant la promotion de la version Ultimate.

Sur Leboncoin, ce sont 62 annonces qui correspondent à cette recherche. Les annonces précisent généralement que le code a déjà été utilisé, et qu’il s’agit uniquement de la boite vide et du poster.
Un acheteur contacté par Frandroid nous indique qu’il s’agit pour lui d’un objet de collection.
Les joueurs que le poster et la boite vide n’intéressent pas peuvent donc récupérer tout de suite une partie du prix du jeu.

articles.chapeau: Le marketing de GTA 6 est extraordinaire dans le sens premier du terme, quitte à aller dans des directions pour le moins curieuses. On a vu Rockstar [...]
articles.txt:
Le marketing de GTA 6 est extraordinaire dans le sens premier du terme, quitte à aller dans des directions pour le moins curieuses. On a vu Rockstar proposer de nouvelles images de son titre dans un épisode de la série South Park , comme si le studio s’auto-parodiait, et il est allé encore un peu plus loin dans l’absurdité en allant proposer à une chaîne météo de jouer le jeu.
La météo peu clémente de Leonida Puisque Rockstar décide de ne rien faire comme les autres, il va chercher la complicité des médias plus grand public pour faire parler de GTA 6, afin de montrer que la sortie du jeu est un événement qui dépasse de loin le simple cadre de l’industrie du jeu vidéo. C’est pourquoi le studio a confié des nouvelles images de son jeu à The Weather Channel, l’équivalent chez nous de Météo-France mais aux États-Unis . Et pas n’importe lesquels, puisqu’il est forcément question de météo.
Sur ces nouvelles images, on y voit les différentes conditions climatiques qui pourront frapper Leonida dans le jeu, que ce soit du brouillard intense ou des tempêtes orageuses. Owen Shepherd, qui s’occupe de l’équipe chargée des rendus de la lumière chez Rockstar Games, déclare :
« Grand Theft Auto VI se déroule à Leonida – un monde fictif inspiré de la Floride contemporaine, avec un paysage doté d’un des systèmes météorologiques les plus imprévisibles des États-Unis. Pour égaler la fidélité de tous les aspects de ce qui est le plus profond et le plus immersif des GTA conçus à ce jour, nous avons dû repenser complètement nos systèmes météorologiques en jeu pour qu’ils paraissent plus localisés, persistants et surtout dynamiques. La météo peut aller de tout, des cieux bleus clairs aux cumulus-nimbus imposants et vertigineux, ancrant les joueurs dans un monde par le biais d’une météo que nous espérons que les habitants de Floride – et les nouveaux visiteurs de Leonida – sauront apprécier. »
Allez, il est temps que toute cette campagne se termine. Rendez-vous ce jeudi pour savourer la météo de Leonida par vous-mêmes.

articles.t: Attention à ce GTA 6 qui circule avant la sortie du jeu : c’est un piège pour voler vos données
articles.chapeau: À deux jours de la sortie de GTA 6, les chercheurs d'Avast ont repéré une arnaque qui promet la version complète du jeu en téléchargement gratuit.
articles.txt:
À deux jours de la sortie de GTA 6, les chercheurs d’Avast ont repéré une arnaque qui promet la version complète du jeu en téléchargement gratuit.
Le jeu le plus attendu de la décennie, GTA VI , débarque ce jeudi sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Un événement mondial pour les joueurs…et les cybercriminels qui tentent de profiter de leur impatience. Spécialiste en sécurité, Avast alerte sur l’existence d’une campagne qui promet de télécharger la version complète du jeu avant tout le monde, et gratuitement.
Une offre évidemment trop belle pour être vraie. À la place du jeu de Rockstar, les victimes récupèrent un logiciel malveillant.
Comme à chaque lancement très attendu, ce type de piège se dévoile. Avast explique que l’arnaque commence par un document PDF soigné, présenté comme un « guide de téléchargement » de GTA 6 , qui reprend les informations officielles sur le jeu, ses personnages et sa date de sortie pour paraître crédible. Un gros bouton « Download now » renvoie vers un site baptisé Getallsoft (ou Getarsoft ou dans le PDF), qui se présente comme une plateforme de téléchargement de logiciels et affirme que GTA 6 y est « disponible en téléchargement gratuit ». En cliquant de nouveau, l’internaute atterrit sur une page imitant Google Drive, qui héberge une archive ZIP de plus de 700 Mo censée contenir le jeu.
Une fois lancé, le contenu de l’archive installe en réalité un infostealer. Ce type de malware est conçu pour aspirer discrètement les données stockées sur l’ordinateur, comme les identifiants et mots de passe enregistrés dans le navigateur, les cookies de session ou encore des informations bancaires, qui sont ensuite revendues ou exploitées par les pirates. Avast avait déjà repéré, il y a quelques semaines, plus de 200 noms de domaine liés à GTA 6 créés en seulement 24 heures. Près de 10 % présentaient un risque élevé ou moyen, à base de fausses précommandes, de sites imitant les boutiques de Rockstar ou de PlayStation, ainsi que de faux jeux-concours.
Pour éviter de tomber dans le piège, un détail suffit pourtant. GTA 6 ne sortira jeudi que sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S, et Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune version PC à ce jour. Un fichier ZIP à installer sur un ordinateur ne peut donc pas contenir le jeu. Même sur console, le téléchargement passe exclusivement par le PlayStation Store ou le Microsoft Store, y compris pour les versions vendues en boîte. Rappelons que ces dernières ne contiennent qu’un code. Enfin, le jeu pèse plus de 200 Go , bien loin des 700 Mo de l’archive proposée par les escrocs.

articles.t: Ils pensent télécharger GTA 6 gratuitement pour PC et finissent avec un virus : attention, les pièges se multiplient à l’approche de la sortie officielle
articles.chapeau: Des arnaqueurs tentent de piéger les joueurs avec un faux guide pour avoir GTA VI gratuitement sur PC (alors que la version PC du jeu n’existe pas encore).
articles.txt:
GTA VI n’intéresse pas que les joueurs. En effet, des hackers et des arnaqueurs en tout genre tentent également de surfer sur l’engouement mondial pour ce titre pour piéger de nouvelles personnes. Et, parmi les arnaques qui circulent sur le web, il y en a une qui promet un accès gratuit au jeu vidéo, sur PC (alors que la sortie du 19 novembre ne concerne encore que les consoles Xbox et PS5). Il s’agit d’une arnaque identifiée par Avast , et relayée par nos confrères de Clubic.
En substance, il y aurait un fichier PDF qui se ferait passer pour un guide pour accéder au jeu. Mais, en faisant passer l’internaute par plusieurs étapes, celui-ci finirait par faire télécharger un logiciel malveillant de type Infostealer, qui peut voler des données sur la machine infectée (ces données peuvent ensuite être utilisées pour lancer des arnaques très crédibles).
Et il ne s’agit que d’un piège parmi d’autres. Dès le mois d’août, Surfshark a, par exemple, identifié la création de plus de 200 noms de domaine sur le thème de GTA 6. Et, sur ces 200 noms de domaines, 57 semblaient avoir été créés pour piéger les joueurs.
“Les noms de domaine eux-mêmes révèlent l’intention : publicité pour de fausses précommandes et pages de paiement, systèmes de cryptomonnaie et de pièces de type « GTA 6 » de type NFT, faux serveurs de jeux, fausses clés bêta et pièges de téléchargement piraté ou gratuit” , expliquait l’entreprise. À l’époque, Surfshark projetait aussi que plus de 750 noms de domaines devraient être créés avant le lancement du 19 novembre.
Selon TechRadar , Surfshark confirme également que des sites frauduleux essaient de piéger les joueurs en promettant un téléchargement du jeu vidéo sur PC, ou même sur mobile.
Malheureusement, pour le moment, on ne sait pas quand la version pour PC de GTA VI sera disponible. En effet, aucune annonce sur ce sujet n’a encore été faite par Rockstar Games. Néanmoins, cette version pour PC pourrait arriver assez rapidement.
Par exemple, d’après un article de Gamesbeat , qui cite des sources proches du dossier, le développeur aurait l’intention de lancer la version PC de GTA VI dès le premier trimestre 2027. De plus, Rockstar Games aurait tout intérêt à se dépêcher, pour éviter que quelqu’un d’autre ne développe lui-même une version PC non officielle du jeu en utilisant l’intelligence artificielle.

articles.txt:
Il ne reste plus qu’une poignée d’heures pour pouvoir enfin jouer à GTA 6 , mais pour certains d’entre vous, l’attente a assez duré. Les plus impatients voudront grappiller chaque minute de plus qui leur permettrait de poser les mains sur le jeu de Rockstar. Heureusement, il existe une solution pour jouer à GTA 6 en avance, et voici comment.
À quelle heure jouer à GTA 6 avec l’astuce de la Nouvelle-Zélande ? Vous le savez probablement, même si vous disposez d’une édition physique de GTA 6 , celle-ci ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement et ne vous laisse préinstaller le jeu avant le jour J. Pour le lancer, il faut attendre le 19 novembre à minuit, heure française , afin que la limitation soit levée. Mais Rockstar a fait le choix de lever cette barrière à minuit, heure locale, dans tous les pays du monde. Ce qui veut dire que le décalage horaire permet une petite astuce.
Celle-ci fonctionne en réalité pour pas mal de jeux et n’est pas exclusive à GTA 6 . Elle est même connue depuis un paquet d’années et s’effectue sans risque de bans ou de sanctions. Pour jouer à GTA 6 en avance, il suffit simplement de paramétrer votre console sur le fuseau horaire de la Nouvelle-Zélande , puisque c’est celui-ci qui aura accès en tout premier au jeu.
Cependant, la PS5 et la Xbox Series ne sont pas logées à la même enseigne et on vous explique pourquoi ainsi que la marche à suivre pour jouer à GTA 6 dès ce mercredi 18 novembre à 12 heures (midi) .
Pour jouer en avance à GTA 6 sur Xbox Series, la manœuvre est assez simple. Il suffit de faire en sorte que votre console soit associée à la région souhaitée, en l’occurrence la Nouvelle-Zélande.
Afin d’y arriver, vous devez effectuer les mesures suivantes :
Vous n’avez pas besoin de changer de compte pour cela, ni de créer un compte Xbox néo-zélandais. Vous pouvez également faire en sorte de conserver la langue française. Une fois le 19 novembre passé, vous pouvez tout à fait replacer votre console sur le fuseau horaire français sans que cela n’impacte votre partie.
Sur PS5, ça se complique. L’astuce de la Xbox Series ne fonctionne pas ici puisque le déblocage dépend du pays de votre compte PSN, et que ce pays ne peut pas être modifié. Vous ne pourrez pas simplement modifier la région de votre console.
Pour pouvoir jouer à GTA 6 en avance, vous devrez tout d’abord vous créer un compte PSN néo-zélandais, en sélectionnant la Nouvelle-Zélande comme pays de résidence lors de la création du compte, puis l’acheter sur le PlayStation Store néo-zélandais (ou en. Ensuite, vous n’aurez accès à GTA 6 que via ce compte, et non via votre compte principal. Si vous collectionnez les trophées ou simplement si vous aimez regrouper tous vos jeux sur un même compte, ce n’est pas l’idéal, même si cela fonctionne quand même.
Est-ce que cela vaut le coup ? On pense que non. Patienter douze heures de plus sur treize longues années d’attente n’est pas un challenge, et cela vous donne l’occasion de jouer à d’autres jeux, voire même de lire quelques articles chez nous comme notre rétrospective sur GTA IV pour faire passer le temps. Mais on vous laisse juges de cela.

An artist for Rockstar described them as “ weirdly invasive ” back then, and it looks like one of the culprits is now facing the consequences. 17-year-old Arion Kurtaj was apprehended for the crime and relegated to custody in a hospital owing to his existing medical conditions. It’s probably welcome news for several of Rockstar’s tireless team members whose efforts risked being undermined by Kurtaj’s actions. Well, let’s hope they put this unfortunate business behind them and bask in the admiration they’ll receive for those dynamic weather systems and everything else they’ve been cooking up for us over the last thirteen years.
We spoke of not being able to believe we’re this close to playing the game a month ago, and that hasn’t really changed, if we’re being honest, even though we’re just a little over a day away from launch. It’s available at midnight local time on November 19th for Xbox Series X/S and PS5.

articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj, 21, pleads guilty to cybercrimes related to the 2022 Rockstar hack and GTA 6 leaks.
articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who first revealed Lucia to the world, has pleaded guilty to cybercrimes in relation to his 2022 hack of Rockstar . He also pleaded guilty to attempting to extort Rockstar, and to attacking workers at a facility where he was being detained after the hack.
Kurtaj, who is now 21, was 17 when he was initially taken into custody over the 2022 Rockstar hack. As he is from the U.K., he could not initially be named as a minor. He was also deemed unable to stand trial due to the severity of his autism, and was instead sent to be held indefinitely in a secure psychiatric facility . Now, as reported by the BBC , he has been deemed able to stand trial and has entered a guilty plea.
The 2022 hack resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw Jason and Lucia for the first time, as they held victims at gunpoint. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. Rockstar refused to pay Kurtaj's ransom.
Crucially, this was our first confirmation that GTA 6 would star a female protagonist, a first in modern GTA games.
It would be over a year before Rockstar finally confirmed this itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year.
It wasn't just the leaked material that brought attention to this hack in 2022, but also the method in which Kurtaj pulled it off. At the time, police were housing him in a hotel after he was apprehended for previous hacks, fearing he would be targeted by rival hackers. Using his hotel TV, an Amazon Fire Stick, and a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, Kurtaj was able to breach Rockstar, taking gameplay clips and files.
Rockstar claims that the hack cost them $5 million to recover from. It further claimed that the Lucia reveal was being kept underwraps for the marketing campaign, something that Kurtaj's leaks spoiled.
However, it isn't just these crimes related to the hack that Kurtaj was facing. The BBC also notes that the 21 year old pleaded guilty to physical assaults, in relation to biting workers at the facility where he was being kept.
Kurtaj is awaiting his sentencing. It is unclear if his time at the secure facility will be taken into account should he recieve a custodial sentence.

articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, the hacker responsible for the massive Grand Theft Auto 6 leak, has pleaded guilty to breaching Rockstar Games and attempting to extort the developer.
The 21-year-old from Oxford admitted the offenses at Woolwich Crown Court on November 16, alongside other cybercrimes committed during his teenage involvement with Lapsus$. His pleas follow an unusual transition from secure psychiatric care to criminal proceedings after doctors reassessed his fitness to stand trial.
The case follows the 2022 arrest linked to the Rockstar and Uber intrusions . Kurtaj attacked Rockstar while on bail for other hacking offenses and staying under police protection at a Travelodge in Bicester. Authorities confiscated his computer, but he used an Amazon Fire Stick connected to the hotel television, along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, to carry out the intrusion.
Kurtaj stole internal company information, including 90 videos containing nearly an hour of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay. He accessed Rockstar’s internal Slack environment and threatened to release source code unless the company contacted him through Telegram within 24 hours.
According to BBC reporting , Rockstar refused to cooperate, and Kurtaj subsequently published stolen material on an online forum using the alias TeaPotUberHacker.
Rockstar estimated its recovery costs at $5 million, alongside thousands of staff hours. The leak also exposed a closely guarded marketing detail: a playable female protagonist.
The incident illustrates how compromised collaboration environments can expose sensitive development assets. However, the precise initial-access mechanism should not be overstated: published analysis distinguishes confirmed Slack access from assessments about credential theft and multifactor authentication fatigue.
In 2023, doctors considered Kurtaj unfit for a conventional criminal trial because of the severity of his autism. A “trial of the facts” therefore asked jurors whether he committed the alleged acts, rather than whether he possessed criminal intent. An indefinite hospital order followed in December 2023. A later assessment found him fit for trial, and he transferred to prison in January.
His admissions also cover attacks against BT/EE, Revolut, and Uber involving social engineering tactics . Prosecutors estimated approximately £10 million in damage across the corporate attacks. They alleged that gang members stole at least $300,000 from cryptocurrency investors. Kurtaj also admitted assaults against custody workers.
The proceedings highlight the operational reach of teenage cybercriminal networks without making their overlapping identities interchangeable.
Analysis of Lapsus$ and related intrusion clusters distinguishes shared personnel and techniques from proof of a single organization. Kurtaj remains in custody awaiting sentencing, bringing renewed attention to identity security, internal access controls, and the business consequences of stolen development data across technology companies and their suppliers worldwide.

articles.chapeau: The Lapsus$ member, initially ruled unfit to stand trial, admitted to the hack that leaked early GTA 6 footage and source code.
articles.txt:
The Lapsus$ member, initially ruled unfit to stand trial, admitted to the hack that leaked early GTA 6 footage and source code.
A hacker behind the 2022 Rockstar Games breach, which led to the leak of unfinished GTA 6 footage and source code, has pleaded guilty to a series of offenses, according to a BBC report .
Arion Kurtaj, a 21-year-old from Oxford, carried out the hack in 2022. He was initially ruled unfit to stand trial because of the severity of his autism and was sentenced to remain in a secure hospital. He was later assessed as fit to stand trial and moved to a regular prison in January. On Monday, he pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and several other offenses, which he committed when he was 16 and 17 as a member of the Lapsus$ hacking gang.
In 2022, Lapsus$ released a 3 GB folder of files and documents related to the development of Rockstar's upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6, revealing the title's work-in-progress gameplay, characters, setting, and more. The group was also responsible for attacking Microsoft , NVIDIA , Uber, and many other companies. After the GTA 6 leak, the group said it had more of Rockstar's confidential documents in its possession and tried to sell GTA 5 and 6's source code , Rockstar's employee details, invoices, and contracts, primarily to Rockstar itself. The studio acknowledged the leak and stated that the "work on the next Grand Theft Auto game will continue as planned". Kurtaj reportedly obtained the game files through a phishing email.
The cyberattack on Rockstar was further investigated by the FBI , which identified two individuals – Kurtaj and an unnamed 17-year-old, described as significant figures within Lapsus$. Following that, Kurtaj was deemed unfit to stand trial.

By: Krishna Goswami New Delhi , Nov 17, 2026 12:25 IST Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 12:25 IST Published by Krishna Goswami Nov 17, 2026 12:25 IST A 21-year-old hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has pleaded guilty to a string of online crimes, including the massive 2022 hack of Rockstar Games that led to the leak of Grand Theft Auto 6. Kurtaj, a key member of the Lapsus$ hacking gang, admitted to his crimes at the Woolwich Crown Court in London on Monday, November 16, 2026.
The guilty plea comes after a highly unusual legal journey. In December 2023, Kurtaj was given an indefinite secure hospital order because doctors believed his severe autism made him unfit to stand a traditional trial.
However, a routine assessment in late 2025 found him fit to face a criminal trial, and he was moved to a standard prison in January 2026. How the GTA 6 hack happened
The way Kurtaj hacked Rockstar Games is quite surprising. In 2022, he was staying at a Travelodge hotel in Bicester under police protection. He was already on bail for other hacking offences, and his laptop had been confiscated by the police.
Despite having no computer, Kurtaj managed to breach Rockstar's systems using just an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room TV, a smartphone, a Bluetooth keyboard, and a mouse.
He stole 90 video clips showing nearly 60 minutes of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay. He then accessed the company's internal Slack messages and threatened to release the game's source code if Rockstar did not contact him on Telegram within 24 hours. When the company refused, he posted the clips on a forum under the username "TeaPotUberHacker".
The leak revealed that GTA 6 would feature its first female playable character, Lucia, a secret Rockstar was closely guarding for marketing purposes. The company stated that recovering from the hack cost them around $5 million and thousands of hours of staff time. Millions in damages and violent behavior
Rockstar Games was not his only victim. Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to hacking Uber , Revolut, and the UK telecom company BT/EE. During the Uber hack, he used social engineering to access internal systems and posted an explicit image of a penis to force the company to pay a ransom.
The court also heard that Kurtaj and the Lapsus$ gang targeted individual cryptocurrency investors, stealing at least $300,000.
His bad behavior continued in custody. Kurtaj pleaded guilty to physically assaulting workers and biting staff multiple times. After being moved to a normal prison, he was caught with a smuggled mobile phone. He used it to send a taunting text message to the police and post updates on Snapchat, which tipped off reporters that he was no longer in the secure hospital. What happens next
Kurtaj stood in the dock on Monday wearing a suit and a buttoned-up white shirt with no tie. He blinked frequently and showed no visible emotion as he confirmed his name and pleaded guilty to all charges, including fraud and unauthorized computer access.
He is scheduled to be sentenced on November 23, 2026. The judge will decide whether he gets a long-term prison sentence or if his mental health history requires him to be sent back under another hospital order.

articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj, 21, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court on November 16 to the September 2022 Rockstar Games breach that leaked 90 GTA VI clips, plus attacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber. articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, the Lapsus$ hacker behind the 2022 leak of GTA 6 footage, has pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games. The 21-year-old from Oxford entered his plea at Woolwich Crown Court in London on Monday, November 16, three days before Rockstar releases the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Kurtaj also admitted to attacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber, which he carried out at the ages of 16 and 17. He further pleaded guilty to assaulting workers while in custody, including several biting incidents. He will be sentenced at the same court on November 23.
Psychiatrists assessed Kurtaj as unfit to stand trial in 2023 because of his autism. A jury at Southwark Crown Court was asked only to decide whether he had committed the acts, and in August 2023 it found he carried out 12 offenses, including three counts of blackmail, two of fraud, and six under the Computer Misuse Act. A mental health assessment presented at his sentencing found he still intended to return to cybercrime as soon as possible.
Kurtaj received a restricted hospital order for an unlimited period in December 2023, which meant he would stay in a secure hospital until doctors judged him no longer a danger. Doctors found him fit to stand trial after a routine assessment in January 2026, and he moved to an ordinary prison to await a fresh hearing. His guilty pleas mean that hearing will not go to trial.
Kurtaj breached Rockstar in September 2022 while on bail for earlier hacks and staying in a Travelodge hotel under police protection. He used an Amazon Fire TV Stick, a smartphone, a keyboard, and a mouse to get in. He then posted in the studio's internal Slack, writing, "I am not a Rockstar employee, I am an attacker," and threatened to start releasing the game's source code unless Rockstar contacted him on Telegram within 24 hours.
Rockstar refused to cooperate. Ninety clips containing nearly 60 minutes of footage from a pre-release build then appeared on a GTA fan forum, more than a year before Rockstar released its first official trailer in December 2023. The clips revealed details, including the game's playable female protagonist, Lucia . Rockstar later told the court the breach cost it $5 million and thousands of hours of staff time.
Prosecutors cast Kurtaj as a leading figure in Lapsus$, a teen-run extortion group that also breached Nvidia , Samsung , and Microsoft in 2021 and 2022. The prosecution estimated damage of around £10 million from his other hacking activities, and his Revolut breach exposed the details of thousands of customers.
A second Lapsus$ member, who was 17 at the time and cannot be named for legal reasons, received a youth rehabilitation order in December 2023 for fraud, Computer Misuse Act and blackmail offenses. GTA 6 launches on November 19 after two delays, first from 2025 and then from May 26, 2026. The standard edition costs $79.99.

articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, the hacker who leaked nearly an hour of unfinished Grand Theft Auto 6 ( GTA 6 ) footage in 2022, pleaded guilty on 16 November to breaching Rockstar Games, three days before the game’s 19 November launch. The 21-year-old from Oxfordshire also admitted attacks on Uber, Revolut, and BT/EE that he carried out at 16 and 17 as a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group.
The pleas, entered at Woolwich Crown Court in London, give Kurtaj his first criminal conviction over the hack. He had been held in a secure hospital under an indefinite order since December 2023, after doctors judged his autism too severe for a conventional trial, but a later assessment found him fit to stand trial and he was moved to an ordinary prison in January.
According to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), Kurtaj admitted three counts of an unauthorised act to impair the operation of a computer, one count of fraud, one count of securing unauthorised access to computer material with intent, and one count of possessing a mobile phone in prison. The hacking offences date from August 2021 to September 2022.
At Uber, Kurtaj sent an explicit image to staff while pressing the company for a ransom, took confidential records, and deleted internal files, causing more than US$2.8 million (£2.1 million) in damage. His breach of Revolut exposed details belonging to thousands of customers. The BT/EE intrusion led to a rise in unauthorised SIM swaps, a scam where criminals trick a phone provider into moving a victim’s number onto a new SIM card, which gives the criminals that person’s calls and texts and a way into their bank and social media accounts.
Reporting from the hearing, the BBC said Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to assaulting staff while in custody, including several biting incidents. Prosecutors cast him as a leading figure in Lapsus$ and told the court the group used data stolen from its corporate targets to go after cryptocurrency investors, taking at least US$300,000 from individuals. Kurtaj’s attacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10 million in damage.
Kurtaj breached Rockstar in September 2022, after he had already been charged over the 2021 BT/EE breach and while on bail over earlier hacks, including one on Nvidia. Police had placed him in a Travelodge in Bicester to protect him from rival hackers who had threatened him over his Bitcoin, and his computer had been confiscated. He kept going anyway, using an Amazon Fire TV Stick plugged into the hotel room’s television, a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, and a mobile phone. That is the conduct the CPS highlighted after the plea, with specialist prosecutor Robert Hutchinson saying Kurtaj kept targeting organisations after being charged, which showed “a persistent disregard for the harm he was causing and the law”.
Prosecutors told his 2023 trial that he got into Rockstar’s systems by posing as a staff member who had lost a password, moving on to a contractor’s account when a former employee’s login failed. Once inside, he took internal data that included 90 clips with nearly an hour of footage from the unfinished GTA 6, then posted on Rockstar’s internal Slack giving the studio 24 hours to contact him on Telegram before he started releasing its source code.
Rockstar refused to cooperate, so Kurtaj posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker. The studio had not yet released the game’s first trailer.
Rockstar has said the breach cost US$5 million (£3.79 million) to recover from, plus thousands of hours of staff time. The studio also said the leak was the first time the public learned that one of GTA 6’s playable characters was a woman, a secret it had been guarding closely for its marketing. That character is Lucia, who shares the lead with Jason and is the first playable female character in the series’ 3D games. The US$5 million covered the clean-up, but it couldn’t give Rockstar a second chance at introducing her, since players first saw Lucia in stolen, unfinished clips instead of a trailer the studio controlled.
Rockstar tightened security after the breach, including a ban on developers working from home, but GTA 6 has leaked again this year. Gameplay videos began surfacing over the summer in a run of leaks Rockstar called “heartbreaking”, and a video released in October included story spoilers. articles.t: Arion Kurtaj GTA 6 Hack: 12 Offenses, $5M Cost
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj did not plead guilty. Found to have done the acts, unfit for trial, hospital order. Rockstar says the GTA 6 hack cost $5M.
articles.txt:
Photo: McPhail, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons A headline making the rounds today says Rockstar Games hacker Arion Kurtaj “pleads guilty” over a $5 million GTA 6 hack. The reporting we can verify tells a different story. Kurtaj was found to have carried out the acts, but he was deemed unfit to stand trial, and the jury was never asked to decide his criminal intent. Beinsure is among the outlets that framed the story as a plea, and that framing is the first thing worth correcting.
The distinction matters more than it looks. With GTA 6 gameplay clips circulating again just days before launch , the 2022 Rockstar intrusion has become the reference case for how a pre-release leak happens and what it costs. Getting the legal status and the dollar figure right is the difference between useful analysis and recycled noise. This piece separates what is confirmed from what is not, then looks at what the case means for studios, publishers and security teams.
Here is the short version. In September 2022, an intruder pulled 90 clips of unreleased GTA 6 footage out of Rockstar’s systems. Kurtaj, then linked to the Lapsus$ group, was found responsible for 12 offenses at Southwark Crown Court. On 21 December 2023 he received an indefinite hospital order. Rockstar told the court the incident cost it $5 million and thousands of hours of recovery work. Nothing in the verified record shows a guilty plea, a prison sentence or a ransom payment of $5 million.

The confirmed record is specific. Arion Kurtaj was 18 at the time of the proceedings. The case was heard at Southwark Crown Court. The jury found that he had carried out the acts alleged, covering 12 offenses that included blackmail, fraud and offenses under the UK Computer Misuse Act. Because he was judged unfit to stand trial, the jury did not rule on whether he intended to commit crimes.
That is a very different outcome from a conviction. In a conventional trial, a jury weighs both the act and the mental state behind it. Here, the question put to jurors was narrower: did the defendant do these things? The answer was yes, and that finding is what the reporting means when it says he was “found responsible.” It is not a guilty verdict, and it is certainly not a guilty plea.
The practical result arrived on 21 December 2023, when Kurtaj received an indefinite hospital order. He was to remain in a secure hospital unless doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. There is no fixed release date attached to that kind of order. Release depends on a clinical judgment rather than a sentence length, which is why you will not find a “years served” figure in any reliable account of the case.
Two things appear to have collided. First, the word “responsible” in court coverage gets compressed by headline writers into “guilty.” Second, aggregator sites often repost a story with fresh timestamps, so a case from 2023 reads as breaking news in November 2026. Neither compression changes the facts. The available reporting does not support a guilty plea, and we are not going to repeat one.
This is not pedantry. A plea implies the defendant accepted responsibility with the capacity to do so. A finding of the acts without a trial implies the opposite: the court judged him unable to take part in the trial. Readers who see “pleads guilty” will assume a prison sentence, a negotiated deal and a closed file. The real situation involves a secure hospital, an open-ended order and a mental-health record that raised concerns about future behavior.
Three questions catch most errors. Did the defendant enter a plea, and if so, when? Did a jury or judge return a verdict on guilt, or only on the facts? And what disposal followed, such as a prison term, a suspended sentence or a hospital order? If a headline cannot answer all three, treat it as incomplete. Applied here, the answers are no plea in the verified record, a finding on the acts only, and an indefinite hospital order.
Reporting ties Kurtaj to Lapsus$, a hacking group whose targets included Rockstar Games, Uber and Nvidia. The group drew attention in 2022 because it went after large, well-resourced companies with methods that did not look like classic ransomware crews. It leaked data publicly, made demands and courted attention, which made its campaigns unusually visible to the press and to security researchers.

--> In London, United Kingdom, 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games' systems in 2022 and publishing early videos from Grand Theft Auto 6. He also admitted to other crimes committed as a teenager while a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group, including an attack on Uber, Engadget reports .
Kurtaj attacked Rockstar while out on bail in another case involving, among other things, the hacking of Nvidia. According to the publication, he carried out a phishing attack using an Amazon Fire TV Stick connected to a television in a hotel room. At the time, he was under police protection due to threats from other hackers.
As a result of the hack, Kurtaj obtained dozens of clips containing nearly an hour of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay. After unsuccessful attempts to blackmail the developer, he published the videos as well as part of the source code.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
In 2023, doctors found Kurtaj unfit to participate in court proceedings due to acute autism. After a jury determined that he had committed the crimes, the court ordered his indefinite hospitalization. In January, he was transferred to a regular prison after it was concluded that he could stand trial.
Kurtaj's sentence will be announced later. Rockstar said that recovering from the 2022 attack cost the company $5 million and thousands of employee work hours. The leak also showed that one of GTA 6's playable characters will be a woman, Lucia, the series' first fully fledged female protagonist.

articles.t: GTA 6 Hacker Pleads Guilty Days Before Game's Release
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak, pleaded guilty to multiple crimes just days before the game's release.
articles.txt:
A little game called Grand Theft Auto VI releases this week, and in a curious quirk of fate, this week also saw Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the 2022 leak of 90 clips containing nearly 60 minutes of footage from a pre-release build of the game, plead guilty to that attack and a bunch of others carried out around the same time.
Kurtaj was in his teens when the attacks were launched; most famously, he cracked Rockstar’s security using only an Amazon Fire Stick, a smart TV, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, doing so from a hotel room in which he was staying while on bail for other attacks. He was duly re-arrested in September 2022 and charged with multiple offences , including fraud, blackmail and computer misuse.
In August 2023, a jury found that Kurtaj had committed the alleged acts , but because doctors had deemed him unfit to stand trial due to his severe autism, the proceedings were limited to determining whether he had carried out the acts rather than whether he was criminally guilty. As the BBC’s Joe Tidy, who has followed the case closely, reported , Kurtaj was subsequently placed under an indefinite hospital order in December 2023, meaning he could remain in a secure hospital for the rest of his life unless authorities determined he was no longer a danger.
That situation changed in January this year after what Tidy described as a “routine assessment.” For reasons that remain unclear—after all, it’s not like someone magically becomes less autistic—Kurtaj was suddenly deemed fit to stand trial and sent to a normal prison to await his day in court. That day arrived this week, and Kurtaj pled guilty to carrying out the Rockstar hack and a string of others, along with several assaults at the aforementioned secure hospital, where he allegedly made a habit of biting workers who got too close to him.
The guilty pleas mean that there’ll be no drawn-out trial, and as of publication, the judgement in the case is yet to be made public, so details of the case are pretty minimal—the court listings for Woolwich Crown Court, where the hearing took place, say only that the hearing is finished. Still, the prosecution managed to outline some spicy details of the hacks, including the fact that “during his hack on Uber, Kurtaj posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.” Delightful.
The guilty pleas mean that there’ll be no drawn-out trial, and Kurtaj is now scheduled to be sentenced on November 23. The court listings confirm that his case was heard at Woolwich Crown Court, while the Crown Prosecution Service has published a detailed account of his offenses. The prosecution also outlined some spicy details of the hacks, including the fact that “during his hack on Uber, Kurtaj posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.” Delightful. Prosecutors said the Uber attack alone cost the company more than $2.8 million.
The Crown Prosecution Service says Kurtaj pleaded guilty to three counts of unauthorized acts impairing a computer’s operation, one count of unauthorized access with intent to commit a further offense, one count of fraud, and one offense involving possession of a mobile phone in prison. His earlier proceedings included blackmail charges, an offense carrying up to 14 years in prison under the Theft Act 1968, but the CPS has not listed a separate blackmail conviction among today’s guilty pleas. Fraud carries a maximum sentence of ten years under the Fraud Act 2006 . And then there are the assault offenses. The BBC reports that Kurtaj pleaded guilty to several assaults on staff while in custody, although the precise charges have not been established. Under UK law, common assault and actual bodily harm are distinct offenses , with different sentencing limits. How much time Kurtaj will actually serve remains to be determined, and the maximum sentences are not necessarily indicative of the punishment he will receive.
Anyway, the tl;dr here is that Kurtaj won’t be hacking anyone any time soon… although, with that said, he did manage to get hold of a mobile phone while in prison in March, from which he posted to Snapchat and, inexplicably, sent a mocking message to the police. For now, he’s back in custody to await sentencing on November 23. How long he’ll remain there—and whether he’ll end up back in a secure hospital—remains to be seen.

Kurtaj used a hotel TV, Amazon Fire Stick and Bluetooth accessories to breach Rockstar in 2022 while on bail, then leaked 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay. Rockstar estimated that the breach cost $5 million and thousands of employee work hours, while prosecutors described Kurtaj as a “leading light” in the hacking group Lapsus$. The hacker behind one of the biggest GTA 6 leaks in history has pleaded guilty to breaching Rockstar Games, years after pulling off a multimillion-dollar cyberattack using little more than a hotel television and an Amazon Fire Stick. Arion Kurtaj, 21, admitted to multiple hacking offenses on Monday, November 16, at Woolwich Crown Court in London after being released from a secure psychiatric hospital earlier this year.
According to the BBC , Kurtaj was transferred from the hospital to a regular prison in January after doctors found him fit to stand trial. He had previously been ordered to remain in secure psychiatric care indefinitely following a 2023 court proceeding.
His latest guilty pleas cover the Rockstar breach and several other cybercrimes he committed at 16 and 17.
The circumstances surrounding the original GTA 6 hack were unusual. In 2022, Kurtaj was staying at a Travelodge hotel in Bicester, England, while on bail for other hacking offenses. Authorities had placed him there for his protection after rival hackers reportedly threatened him over stolen Bitcoin.
Despite having his computer confiscated, Kurtaj accessed Rockstar's systems using an Amazon Fire Stick connected to the hotel television, along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
Once inside, Kurtaj obtained internal company information, including 90 clips containing nearly an hour of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay. He also accessed Rockstar's internal Slack messaging system and issued an ultimatum: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours, I will start releasing the source code."
Kurtaj subsequently published the stolen material online under the username TeaPotUberHacker, exposing gameplay footage and revealing that the upcoming title would feature a female playable protagonist.
Rockstar later estimated that the breach cost approximately $5 million to address, in addition to thousands of employee work hours.
Prosecutors described Kurtaj as a "leading light" in Lapsus$, a hacking group responsible for attacks against major companies including Uber, Revolut and telecommunications provider BT/EE.
The group's activities reportedly caused approximately £10 million in damage, while prosecutors alleged its members stole at least $300,000 from cryptocurrency investors.
Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to assaulting workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents. Authorities previously discovered he had obtained a mobile phone in prison after he sent a taunting message to police and posted on Snapchat.
The guilty pleas mark another chapter in Rockstar's long-running battle with unauthorized GTA 6 disclosures. The company has faced additional leaks and threats from hackers as it prepares to release the game, currently scheduled for November 19.
Kurtaj's former Lapsus$ associate, Thalha Jubair, was separately sentenced to five years and six months in prison after continuing his cybercriminal activities with another group.

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.
The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.
At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.
As the BBC reports , he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.
Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.
"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. Cybercriminals attempt to cash in on the hype around the game, luring fans with malware-laced downloads and ‘early access’ that doesn’t exist
On November 19 th , 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI will be released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. But cybercriminals aren’t waiting for launch day. They have long been capitalizing on the hype around what’s arguably the most anticipated game of the decade, using fake leaks, malware-laced downloads, bogus online stores with rock-bottom prices, and fraudulent “early access” schemes to lure eager fans. Security experts at ESET expect such scams to proliferate as the release approaches and the holiday shopping season gets underway.
It’s easy to see why the franchise makes such an attractive lure: Grand Theft Auto is one of the most successful entertainment properties of all time, with more than 470 million units sold worldwide, according to Rockstar Games. Before taking a closer look at the scams tied to GTA VI, let’s establish what Rockstar has actually announced.
Pre-orders opened on June 25 th . According to Rockstar Games’ official pre-order announcement , the Standard Edition is priced at $79.99 in the United States, while the Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. Players who pre-order a digital copy have been able to pre-load the game since November 10 th .
What Rockstar has not announced is just as important, particularly with so many fraudulent offers circulating online: there is currently no official beta, playable demo, or early-access program that would let players start playing GTA VI before release day.
Nor has Rockstar announced a PC version, PC release date, or system requirements. This makes the official information a useful reality check: offers built around a supposed PC version, beta, demo, or early access are promising something Rockstar has never confirmed.

Le sondage est apparu à 14 h 39 dans l’interface publique, après le message annonçant une nouvelle fuite pour le 28 octobre 2026.
L’affaire Cyberleek n’est peut-être pas terminée. Après avoir annoncé le 14 octobre dernier mettre fin à ses divulgations concernant GTA 6, le mystérieux auteur ou collectif semble avoir changé d’avis.
Un communiqué intitulé “ RETURN OF CL “, daté du 21 octobre, est apparu sur le site associé à ses précédentes publications. Le message promet un retour particulièrement offensif, avec de nouvelles révélations dont la nature reste inconnue.
Cette annonce intervient à moins d’un mois de la sortie du jeu. Le titre est attendu le 19 novembre 2026.

According to reporting on the release, the footage shows short clips centered on Lucia, one of GTA 6’s two confirmed protagonists, moving through a barbershop, taking part in a shop robbery, lounging by a pool, and passing through assorted map locations, capped by flyover footage of the game world. Cyberleek described these as pulled from the game’s final missions. That claim has not been independently verified, and separate reporting notes the footage does not clearly establish a connection to a final mission or show anything resembling an actual ending cutscene.
That distinction matters more than it might seem. Dexerto’s coverage of the release framed it as Cyberleek posting “parts of final missions” while stopping the broader leak campaign, a characterization that leaves plenty of room between what was shown and what was promised. Eurogamer’s report on the same video used similarly careful language, describing the clips as allegedly showing scenes from the final mission while noting the leaks may have come to an end rather than stating outright that they have. The gap between “allegedly” and “confirmed” is the entire story here, and it’s one Rockstar has done nothing to close.
Cyberleek’s message accompanying the video leaned on two phrases that have since been repeated across gaming coverage: “The leeks stop here. For now.” and “The ending stays unpublished.” Read together, those lines do two things at once. They announce a halt to new leaks while deliberately leaving the door open with “for now,” and they draw a hard line around the one piece of content Cyberleek says it will withhold regardless of what happens next, the actual ending.
That second phrase is worth sitting with. If the campaign really does have footage beyond what’s been shown, holding back the ending is the one piece of leverage that survives a collapsed token. Whether that leverage is real or just the last card in a bluff is exactly what nobody outside Cyberleek’s circle can confirm. Enduins, one of the outlets tracking the saga closely, titled its own report on the episode “Cyberleek Ends GTA VI Leaks After Memecoin Collapses,” tying the stoppage directly to the token’s crash rather than treating it as a planned conclusion.
The numbers behind $CYBERLEEK tell a familiar story to anyone who has watched a thin-liquidity memecoin move. The token reportedly climbed to a peak market capitalization of $7.8 million on October 11, 2026, the same week Cyberleek was promising bigger disclosures tied to higher valuations. articles.txt:
La communauté du jeu vidéo a récemment été secouée par le retour inattendu de Cyberleek , cette entité anonyme qui avait pris l’habitude de divulguer des informations sensibles concernant les développements internes de Rockstar Games. Après plusieurs jours de silence relatif, ce leaker prolifique a réapparu avec une nouvelle plateforme web et des images inédites tirées de la mission finale de Grand Theft Auto VI .
Cette résurgence soudaine relance le débat éthique autour du piratage numérique et de la préservation de l’expérience joueur, tout en soulevant des questions persistantes quant aux motivations financières derrière ces actions spectaculaires. Les joueurs se demandent désormais si cette promesse de cessation définitive sera tenue ou s’il ne s’agit que d’un artifice marketing supplémentaire destiné à alimenter la spéculation autour des actifs cryptographiques associés.
Contrairement aux précédentes divulgations massives incluant des heures de gameplay brut, Cyberleek a opté pour une approche chirurgicale en publiant exclusivement des séquences de la dernière mission du titre très attendu. L’objectif affiché était de préserver le plaisir de découverte des futurs acheteurs tout en maintenant une pression médiatique maximale sur l’éditeur Take-Two Interactive.
Le leaker a explicitement mentionné détenir les fichiers relatifs à la conclusion narrative globale du jeu mais a choisi de ne pas les diffuser publiquement. Cette décision repose sur un calcul froid : publier la fin aurait causé des dommages irréparables à l’expérience utilisateur, tandis que la retenue actuelle permet de maintenir une forme de levier sans franchir le seuil critique de la ruine totale. La stratégie semble donc évoluer vers une nuisance contrôlée plutôt qu’une destruction ouverte, bien que les intentions profondes restent sujettes à caution.
À LIRE AUSSI : Neuf nouveaux jeux rejoignent le catalogue PlayStation Plus en octobre 2026
Les observateurs avisés ont rapidement noté la coïncidence temporelle entre ces nouvelles fuites et la promotion active d’un jeton numérique non-fongible baptisé « CL ». Cyberleek rejette catégoriquement toute accusation de spéculation financière pure, qualifiant le token de simple outil de collecte de dons destinés à financer ses activités futures.
Néanmoins, la corrélation directe entre la visibilité accrue apportée par les leaks et la capitalisation boursière volatile de ce meme-coin suggère une dynamique économique sous-jacente indéniable. Le leaker accuse les sceptiques, notamment certains créateurs de contenu YouTube, de cynisme aveugle face à sa prétendue démarche philanthropique envers la communauté des joueurs.
Il affirme agir pour protéger l’intégrité du divertissement contre les abus corporatifs, tout en exploitant paradoxalement l’écosystème spéculatif des cryptomonnaies pour soutenir son infrastructure technique coûteuse et complexe.
Au cœur de cette saga digitale se trouve un mystérieux projet parallèle, distinct de Rockstar, nécessitant des ressources matérielles considérables et une durée de développement estimée à plusieurs années. Pour concrétiser cette ambition, Cyberleek avait conditionné la publication d’une build complète du jeu au franchissement d’un palier symbolique de trente millions de dollars en capitalisation boursière du memecoin associé.
Cet objectif ambitieux n’a jamais été atteint, la valeur du jeton stagnants autour d’un million de dollars seulement. Face à cet échec financier cuisant, le leaker a annoncé honorer ses engagements contractuels implicites en refusant de télécharger anonymement plus de deux cents gigaoctets de données risquées.
Cette posture rigide masque mal une déception profonde vis-à-vis d’une audience jugée trop frileuse pour soutenir pleinement ses initiatives audacieuses et potentiellement lucratives.
À LIRE AUSSI : Rockstar garantit un développement plus rapide pour son prochain titre
Malgré les promesses solennelles de retrait définitif formulées dans le communiqué officiel, la prudence demeure de mise parmi les analystes du secteur vidéoludique. Avec encore plus d’un mois avant la sortie officielle de Grand Theft Auto VI , il paraît improbable que cette source d’information cesse totalement ses activités perturbatrices.
Le style rédactionnel particulier, marqué par une utilisation excessive de la voix passive et une structure syntaxique hachée, confirme la continuité de l’auteur principal derrière ces publications successives.

articles.t: GTA VI Developers Showed a "Black Mark" to Hacker Cyberleek? A Threat from Rockstar Was Seen in the Trailer
articles.chapeau: Some players are sure that the developers left a "signal" for the hacker.
articles.txt:
Some players are sure that the developers left a "signal" for the hacker.
Until recently, a hacker (or group) under the nickname Cyberleek actively published Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay footage online and also threatened to leak a build with the full story. However, he then reconsidered his decision and abandoned further leaks.
Soon after, Rockstar Games released the Grand Theft Auto VI trailer. Fans began to examine the footage, and a moment with a green car attracted attention. Those who closely followed the leaks immediately recognized it — it appeared in Cyberleek's videos.
1 / 2 Image source: Rockstar Games In the trailer, this model can be seen at the 0:46 mark — the driver is trying to escape from the police. Players believe that the appearance of this car is not a random coincidence. It is assumed that in this way, the developers from Rockstar Games sent a warning signal to Cyberleek to prevent further possible leaks.
Discussion participants recalled how in one of the Grand Theft Auto VI trailers, the opening scene with Jason began with him saying he was fixing some leaks (in the Russian subtitles, the phrase “fixing some leaks” was translated as “just fixing the roof,” so some Russian-speaking players might have missed the reference). During that period, hackers were leaking internal studio materials.
Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for release on November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles.

articles.t: Cyberleek's 3-Part Message Ends GTA 6 Leaks [2026]
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek posted a three-part End of the road message on Oct 14, 2026, ending its GTA 6 leak campaign without a PC build or spoilers.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the anonymous account behind months of Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, says it is done. On October 14, 2026, the leaker posted a three-part message titled “End of the road,” announcing it will not release a full game build, will not post the game’s ending, and does not plan further early gameplay leaks. The post marks the clearest signal yet that the long-running GTA 6 leak saga, which has rattled Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive for the better part of a year, may finally be winding down.
Whether that holds is a separate question. Cyberleek has reversed course before, and its claimed access to a development build and to the game’s ending, made on October 13 and 14, 2026, has not been independently confirmed. The message itself said only that the leaks had stopped “for now.” Still, the announcement reframes a leak campaign that previously threatened to dump an entire playable build onto torrent sites. Instead, the leaker is walking away, at least for now, while keeping a handful of final-mission clips online as what it calls proof of access.

According to the October 14 post, Cyberleek broke its farewell statement into three distinct parts. The first addressed the fate of the alleged full game build, the second covered the ending and story content, and the third offered a handful of final clips described as proof rather than spoilers. Kotaku reported on the message under the headline “GTA 6 Leaker Announces They Won’t Release The Full Game” , framing it as the leaker calling a stop to the campaign, at least for the time being.
Cyberleek had previously floated a conditional threat: if a crypto token tied to the account hit a $30 million market cap, the full build would go out, story mode included, all the way to the credits. In its own words from that earlier post, “Here’s the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out, full story mode, played to the end, credits and all,” as Gadgets360 reported at the time. That target was never reached, and the October 14 message closes the loop on it.
Cyberleek’s stated reasoning centers on risk versus reward. Uploading a claimed 200+ GB playable build anonymously, a release Mashable reported Cyberleek threatened on October 12, 2026, carries real exposure. PCMag reported the playable build was advertised as over 200GB in October 2026, and Mashable reported that an alleged development build was offered behind a $40 paywall that same month. The leaker framed the payoff as only worth it if the associated cryptocurrency reached its $30 million market-cap target and funded whatever project sat behind the threat. With the target missed, the math apparently stopped working. The account has made no claim about a PC build timeline, pricing, or file size beyond what it has already posted, and none of those specifics are confirmed by any outlet covering the story.
This is a notable shift from the tone Cyberleek struck in earlier posts, which read more like negotiation tactics aimed at Take-Two than a farewell. Eurogamer covered the escalation at the time the full-build threat first surfaced, and the contrast between that posture and the October 14 retreat is stark. Readers can track the earlier claim in shattered.io’s own coverage of Cyberleek’s 200GB “playable” build claim , which laid out the scope of what the leaker said it was holding.
The second part of the message dealt specifically with the game’s ending, and it’s arguably the most consequential piece of the whole statement. Cyberleek claims to have access to the conclusion of GTA 6’s story but says it will not publish it. In its own words, reported by Kotaku, “CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly, but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy, why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished.”
That framing matters because it draws a line between punishing a publisher and punishing the people who bought the game. Cyberleek positions itself as drawing that line deliberately, rather than being forced into it. No outlet has confirmed whether the claimed ending footage actually exists, and Take-Two has not addressed the claim directly.
